hints: Focus on the word decreases. Ask yourself, which feature would give the pathogen less time or less opportunity to pass from one person to water to another person?
Think about the trade-off for a pathogen: a live, moving host who sheds bacteria spreads disease, while a host who dies very quickly cannot keep spreading it.
walkthrough:
**What helps a pathogen spread?**

Think like the bacterium for a moment. To spread, Vibrio cholerae needs a living host who moves around and sheds bacteria in faeces into water supplies.

Anything that keeps hosts alive, mobile, and unnoticed will increase spread. Anything that removes hosts quickly will decrease spread.

**Test each feature against that idea**

Short-lived immunity means people soon become susceptible again, so that helps spread. Symptomless carriers feel well, so they move, work and mix normally while shedding bacteria, so that greatly helps spread.

Successful treatment keeps people alive longer, so they also have more time to shed bacteria if hygiene is poor.

**Spot the one that limits spread**

Option C says untreated symptomatic cholera rapidly kills up to 50% of people. A dead host cannot move, cannot travel, and stops shedding new bacteria.

That rapid death removes sources of infection from the population, so even though it is tragic, it decreases further transmission. That makes C the answer.

options.A: Short-lived vaccine immunity means more susceptible people sooner, which would increase, not decrease, spread.
options.B: 98% symptomless carriers feel healthy and move freely while shedding bacteria, which greatly increases silent spread.
options.C: Rapid death of up to 50% of untreated symptomatic patients removes hosts quickly, giving the pathogen less time to be transmitted to others.
options.D: Successful rehydration keeps 99% of patients alive, so they survive longer and can continue to shed bacteria, which does not decrease spread.
